subject: intermediate step between Rmd and html or pdf?

messages.author: 4f6f5f995ee31178
messages.subject: intermediate step between Rmd and html or pdf?
parts:
I'm starting to use knitr, mainly through spin() and find it very useful.
I'm just missing what I would call an intermediate step in which the R code
were already executed but you could still fine tune the formatting of
the text. Is this possible? In some cases, parts of my R code take
a bit long time and then when I see the html or the pdf
I realize that a given title should actually be a sub-title or
I would prefer to have some terms in italics. In those cases I have to
go back to the script and besides making these minor changes also have to re-run the R code.

Thanks for any suggestion on this matter,

Agus

messages.author: 8502567f9dbc7c7e
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] intermediate step between Rmd and html or pdf?
parts: Separate your calculations from presentation. I usually put my input and processing steps into an R file. Then I create an R file where I setup any calculation parameters, source the calculations file, and use save.image() to store the results. Then I create the Rnw file that re-loads any needed libraries and uses the load() function to pull the results into memory, and the rest of the Rnw file renders the output. As I refine my calculations I move more and more of them into functions that produce objects and fewer global variables are used. This allows me to store result sets into lists and use knitr templates to render multiple calculation cases.

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] intermediate step between Rmd and html or pdf?
parts:
But remember that it is not easy to merge the changes in the
intermediate files back to the source files. Once you touch the
*.tex/*.md output, it is expensive to buy a "return ticket", unless
you do not want to go back at all. If some code chunks are very
time-consuming, you can consider caching or the old plain
save()/load() method.

Regards,
Yihui
